clue.text: Where guys might secure temporary accommodation?

definitions.text: Where guys might secure temporary accommodation

parts.words: Where guys might secure temporary accommodation?
parts.note: surface reading: a place where some men could find a short-term room
setter's reading: guy ropes, the lines that hold a tent firmly to the ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Guys' reads as men, but guy ropes are what pin down a tent, the temporary accommodation in question.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitch for tents is a place where guy ropes are pegged to hold up a camper's shelter.

clue.text: Colour of tree with leaves

indicators.note: something that leaves departs, so the abbreviation just before this verb goes out of the word

parts.note: the rowan is the mountain ash
W is the standard abbreviation for with

explanation.surface: Someone asks what shade a tree turns once it has its foliage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With leaves' looks like foliage, but it means the W for 'with' departs from the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: Roan is a horse's coat colour where white hairs are mixed through a darker base.

clue.text: Lacier pants — sweet!

indicators.note: pants is slang for rubbish, so the preceding word is badly made and must be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An exclamation of delight about some extra-lacy underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pants' looks like a noun for underwear; in British slang it also means rubbish, which signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a cream-filled choux pastry, a kind of sweet treat or dessert.

clue.text: You and I agree to remove article on rising damp

parts.note: you and I together are we

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, from bottom to top
removing an article means taking the little word 'a' out of the word for agree

parts.note: to assent is to agree
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Two people agree to clear something away when damp starts creeping up a wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising damp' looks like a single phrase about walls, but rising is the reversal signal and damp alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Damp used as a noun is moisture, the condition of being wet.

clue.text: Flat in Little Venice

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the words that follow, spanning the gap between them

parts.note: the last letter of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An apartment in Little Venice, a canal-side district of west London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flat' looks like an apartment, but it is the adjective meaning level.
explanation.definitionFit: Even and flat both describe a surface that is level and smooth, without bumps.

clue.text: Having been stopped by spies, revolutionary on a list reluctant to join party

indicators.note: being stopped by something means having it plugged into your middle
a revolutionary overturns the order, so the words after it are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A radical on a watch list, intercepted by intelligence agents, is unwilling to join a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party' suggests politics, but the definition means a social gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone antisocial avoids company and would rather not attend social gatherings.

clue.text: In conclusion, left much to be uncovered

indicators.note: in a down clue the cover is the top, so uncovering removes the first letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
vastly means very much

explanation.surface: Someone ends by saying a great deal remains to be revealed.
explanation.definitionFit: Lastly is the adverb used to introduce a final point, as in finally.

clue.text: Carriage with no covering inspires pained expression

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the first word takes the second inside it

parts.note: something with no covering is bare
the cry when something hurts

explanation.surface: An open carriage ride prompts someone to wince.
explanation.definitionFit: A barouche is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding hood, popular in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Very old South American flower

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
the Inca empire ruled the Andes before the Spanish conquest

explanation.surface: An ancient bloom from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinca is the botanical genus of periwinkle, a trailing plant with blue or white blossoms.

clue.text: In contact with company ignoring voucher

indicators.note: ignoring something leaves it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: a coupon is a voucher
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A firm in touch with a customer refuses to honour their voucher.
explanation.definitionFit: The preposition means on, resting against or touching a surface, as in placed on a table.

clue.text: Proclaim ancient sauna with no walls needs development

indicators.note: developing something changes its form, so the collected letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: walls are the outer edges, so taking them away keeps just the inner letters

parts.note: the word minus its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Someone announces that a crumbling old sauna lacking walls needs redeveloping.
explanation.definitionFit: To annunciate is an older form of announce, to declare publicly or formally.

clue.text: Flexible measure of obesity adopted by relative in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the combined letters are read backwards
something adopted is taken in, so the measure goes inside the relative

parts.note: REL is a short form of relative
body mass index

explanation.surface: A retired relative stays supple while taking up a weight index.
explanation.walkthrough: The insertion happens first; only then is the whole combination turned round, so the relative's letters end up at both ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Limber as an adjective means supple and lithe, able to bend easily.

clue.text: A tiny amount of dough raised?

definitions.text: A tiny amount of dough raised?

parts.words: A tiny amount of dough raised?
parts.note: surface reading: very little money collected
setter's reading: dough that has risen and been baked into a loaf, of which a tiny bit is the item

explanation.walkthrough: Dough is slang for money, so 'raised' looks like fundraising; really it is risen dough baked into a loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny fragment broken off a baked loaf is the smallest piece of leavened dough.

clue.text: Returning a little sexy nod, rascal produces gemstone

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the run of letters is read right to left
a little of the following words means only a run of their letters is used

parts.note: letters spanning the three words

explanation.surface: A cheeky fellow answers a flirty nod with a jewel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sardonyx is a banded variety of onyx with layers of sard, prized as a gem for cameos.

clue.text: Line catching Australian fish

indicators.note: catching something holds it inside, so the line takes in the letter

parts.note: RY is the abbreviation for railway, a line
A is the abbreviation for Australian

explanation.surface: A fishing line hooks something from Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' sounds like fishing tackle; here it is a railway line.
explanation.definitionFit: Rays are flat cartilaginous sea creatures with wide wing-like fins, such as stingrays.

clue.text: Criminal enterprise will ultimately scare grasses

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order
ultimately points to the final letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: the final letter of each word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A gang's racket will in the end frighten informers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grasses' looks like British slang for informers; here it is the plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereals such as wheat, oats and barley are cultivated members of the grass family.

clue.text: Rebellious princess denied introduction to Alex Garland

indicators.note: denied means refused, so that letter is taken away from the princess

parts.note: Princess Leia leads the Rebel Alliance in Star Wars

indicators.note: an introduction comes first, so only the opening letter of the name is taken

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A film-world snippet: a rebel princess is refused an introduction to director Alex Garland.
explanation.walkthrough: Alex Garland reads as one name, the film director, but the surname is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lei is a Hawaiian wreath of flowers worn around the neck.

clue.text: Mock orange leader of nationalist government visiting country bordering Israel

indicators.note: a visitor goes inside a place, so these letters are placed within the country

parts.note: Syria lies to the north-east of Israel
G is the abbreviation for government

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so the first letter of the following word is kept

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: A nationalist leader and his government make a visit to a neighbouring state, with a sneer at orange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mock' looks like a verb but is part of the plant's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Syringa is a common name for philadelphus, the shrub known as mock orange for its scented white blossoms.

clue.text: Around noon, welcome unlimited meat and drink

indicators.note: around says the next letter is wrapped by the word for welcome

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
N is the abbreviation for noon

indicators.note: without limits means the outer boundary letters are lost, keeping the inside

parts.note: the word minus its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A lunchtime offer: an all-you-can-eat buffet with drinks around midday.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is a drink brewed from unfermented tea leaves, popular in East Asia.

clue.text: One who's not fully paid son for clothing label

indicators.note: clothing something covers it, so the pair of pieces wraps around the record label

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
pro means in favour of
EMI is a well-known record label

explanation.surface: A parent complains a son isn't paid in full by a fashion brand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clothing label' reads as a fashion brand; really clothing is the wrap and the label is musical.
explanation.definitionFit: A semi-professional earns some money from a sport or activity but not a full living.

clue.text: How long it takes to produce heavy metal magazine

definitions.text: How long it takes to produce

parts.note: lead is a famously dense metal
Time is an American news magazine

explanation.surface: A question about the schedule for publishing a heavy metal music magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heavy metal' looks like rock music; it is literally a heavy element.
explanation.definitionFit: Lead time is the interval between ordering or starting something and its completion or delivery.

clue.text: Puzzle in game's complicated

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled, so the letters are mixed into another order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A conundrum within a game is intricate.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling that needs to be worked out.

clue.text: European capital previously sent back some abandoned luggage

indicators.note: sending something back returns it the way it came, so read right to left
some means only part of the following words, a continuous run of letters

parts.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Some unattended bags at a European capital's airport were returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city such as Amsterdam, but here it means money.
explanation.definitionFit: The gulden, or guilder, was the Dutch currency until the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Man who's kept freelance job heading off on his own

indicators.note: with its heading off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a gig is a one-off paid engagement
solo means alone

explanation.surface: A man whose freelance work dried up is living alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A gigolo is a man financially supported by a lover, usually an older wealthy woman.

clue.text: Looking at speaking up about inflationary measure in recession

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first word goes around the measure

parts.note: a side that is up is ahead in the game

indicators.note: a recession is a going back, so the measure is read backwards

parts.note: the Retail Prices Index, a British measure of inflation

explanation.surface: An economist speaks about inflation during a recession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' here means winning, as a team two goals up is in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Lip-reading means understanding talk by watching the movements of the mouth, so it is watching words.

clue.text: Help criminal President Trump initially

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, the US president

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so only the first letter of the name is used

parts.note: the opening letter

explanation.surface: An accusation that a president was aided in wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Trump' reads as one name; the president is Lincoln and Trump only provides a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to assist or encourage someone in committing a crime.

clue.text: School touring northern lake

indicators.note: touring goes round a place, so the school surrounds the letter

parts.note: a pod is a school of whales or dolphins
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A school party takes a trip to a lake in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like pupils on a trip; it is a group of sea mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond is a small body of still water, a little lake.

clue.text: Academic test essentially lacking

indicators.note: lacking its essence means the very central letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a proof is a test, as in 'the proof of the pudding'

explanation.surface: A scholar's exam is found fundamentally wanting.
explanation.definitionFit: Prof is the informal short form of professor, a senior university academic.

clue.text: Short of time, playwright pens second part for Beerbohm Tree

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the playwright's name holds the next letter
short of means lacking, so that letter is taken off the playwright's name

parts.note: David Mamet, American playwright of Glengarry Glen Ross
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: the second part of the following name is its second letter

parts.note: the second letter

explanation.surface: A rushed dramatist writes a role for Herbert Beerbohm Tree, the Victorian actor-manager.
explanation.walkthrough: Beerbohm Tree looks like one name, the actor; Tree alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamee, or mammee apple, is a tropical American tree grown for its edible fruit.

clue.text: Chance to win big old car without endless charges

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the car goes around
without its ends, the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Rover was a British car maker, now defunct
tolls are charges for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: A vintage car could win a big prize if it avoids fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' looks like lacking, but here it means outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery rollover is a jackpot carried forward unwon, so the next draw offers an extra-large prize.
